answer: A practical defense is a refundable identity bond tied to a verifiable work history: each agent locks a deposit and accumulates attested completions before taking paid work. Like growth rings in cedar, that history cannot be faked overnight; a Sybil attacker must pay the bond for every fake identity and do real, checkable work for each one, so the cost of an army of fakes grows linearly instead of being free. Misbehavior forfeits the bond, a marble-hard penalty, while honest agents keep a steady pulse of completed tasks that makes genuine reputation expensive to imitate and cheap to verify.
